Define the pre-specified MMRM to stress-test

Source: R/spec.R
stress_spec.Rd

A stress_spec holds the analysis data and every decision of the pre-specified mixed model for repeated measures: the response, subject, visit and treatment variables, the covariates, the visit at which the treatment contrast is taken, the within-subject covariance structure, the degrees-of-freedom method, the variance estimator and the significance level. Every family function in the package takes a spec and returns rows in the schema of stress_fit().

Usage

stress_spec(
  data,
  response,
  subject,
  visit,
  treatment,
  reference = NULL,
  active = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  contrast_visit = NULL,
  covariance = "us",
  method = "Kenward-Roger",
  vcov = "Kenward-Roger-Linear",
  alpha = 0.05,
  weights = c("equal", "observed"),
  label = "pre-specified",
  sas_conventions = TRUE,
  time = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, one row per subject and visit.

response

Name of the response column (change from baseline, say).

subject

Name of the subject identifier column.

visit

Name of the visit column; coerced to a factor whose level order is the visit order.

treatment

Name of the treatment column (two or more arms).

reference

The reference (control) level of treatment. Defaults to the first factor level.

active

The treatment level compared with the reference. Defaults to the first non-reference level. With three or more arms, change it with spec_update() to stress-test each comparison in turn.

covariates

Fixed-effect covariates besides treatment and visit, as a one-sided formula (~ base + site) or a character vector of term labels. Character and logical columns are treated as class variables.

contrast_visit

The visit level at which the treatment contrast is estimated. Defaults to the last visit level.

covariance

Covariance structure name as used by mmrm: "us", "ar1", "ar1h", "cs", "csh", "toep", "toeph", "ad", "adh", or "sp_exp" (spatial exponential, the SAS SP(POW) structure, on the continuous time variable).

method

Degrees-of-freedom method passed to mmrm::mmrm_control(): "Satterthwaite", "Kenward-Roger", "Residual" or "Between-Within".

vcov

Variance estimator passed to mmrm::mmrm_control(): "Asymptotic", "Empirical", "Empirical-Jackknife", "Empirical-Bias-Reduced", "Kenward-Roger" or "Kenward-Roger-Linear". The SAS DDFM=KR default corresponds to method = "Kenward-Roger" with vcov = "Kenward-Roger-Linear".

alpha

Two-sided significance level.

weights

How class covariates are weighted in the least-squares means: "equal" (every level equally, SAS LSMEANS default) or "observed" (the design is averaged over the covariate values of the analysis rows, as SAS OBSMARGINS and g-computation do).

label

Label for the base analysis in output rows.

sas_conventions

If TRUE, the between-within degrees of freedom for a sandwich-variance contrast are computed as SAS PROC MIXED does when EMPIRICAL is combined with a DDFM it cannot honour (observations minus subjects minus the rank of the within-subject design columns).

time

Name of a numeric time column for the "sp_exp" structure (days from randomisation, say; mmrm converges more readily with time rescaled to hundreds of days).

Value

An object of class stress_spec.

Details

The fixed effects are covariates + treatment + visit + treatment:visit; the treatment contrast at contrast_visit is the difference of least-squares means (active minus reference) with class covariates weighted equally over their levels and continuous covariates at their means, the convention of SAS LSMEANS.

Examples

spec <- stress_spec(mmrm::fev_data, response = "FEV1", subject = "USUBJID",
                    visit = "AVISIT", treatment = "ARMCD", reference = "PBO",
                    covariates = ~ RACE + SEX + FEV1_BL, contrast_visit = "VIS4")
spec
#> <stress_spec> pre-specified
#>   data:       800 rows, 200 subjects, visits VIS1 VIS2 VIS3 VIS4
#>   model:      FEV1 ~ RACE + SEX + FEV1_BL + ARMCD + AVISIT + ARMCD:AVISIT + us(AVISIT | USUBJID)
#>   contrast:   TRT - PBO at VIS4
#>   inference:  Kenward-Roger df, Kenward-Roger-Linear vcov, alpha 0.05
